question: Which article of the Indian constitution provides freedom to manage its own affairs in matters of religion?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 26.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Article 26 of the Indian Constitution grants every religious denomination (or any section of it) the freedom to manage its own affairs in matters of religion. (धार्मिक मामलों के प्रबंधन की स्वतंत्रता)

• Subject to public order, morality and health, Article 26 gives every religious denomination the right:

◦ (a) to establish and maintain institutions for religious and charitable purposes;

◦ (b) to manage its own affairs in matters of religion;

◦ (c) to own and acquire movable and immovable property;

◦ (d) to administer such property in accordance with law.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Article 21 guarantees the Right to Life and Personal Liberty — no person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law.

• Article 37 falls under Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy) and declares that the Directive Principles are not enforceable by any court but are fundamental in the governance of the country.

• Article 15 prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.

NOTE

• The Right to Freedom of Religion is covered by Articles 25 to 28:

◦ Article 25 — freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion

◦ Article 26 — freedom to manage religious affairs

◦ Article 27 — freedom from payment of taxes for promotion of any particular religion

◦ Article 28 — freedom from attending religious instruction in certain educational institutions

question: If Birth rate of a country is more than death rate then the population will ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is increase.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Natural growth of population = Birth rate − Death rate. When the birth rate exceeds the death rate, the natural growth rate is positive, so the population increases. (जनसंख्या में वृद्धि होगी)

• Birth rate is the number of live births per 1,000 people in a year; death rate (mortality rate) is the number of deaths per 1,000 people in a year.

◦ Example: If the birth rate is 20 per 1,000 and the death rate is 7 per 1,000, the natural growth rate is 13 per 1,000, i.e. 1.3 per cent annual growth.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• If the death rate is higher than the birth rate, the population declines (as in Japan and several European countries today).

• If the two rates are equal, the population remains stationary in natural terms.

• Actual population change also depends on migration: Population change = (Births − Deaths) + (Immigration − Emigration).

NOTE

• India's population growth is studied through the Census (held every 10 years; the last completed census was in 2011) and the Sample Registration System (SRS) of the Registrar General of India.

• The demographic transition theory explains how societies move from high birth and death rates to low birth and death rates as they develop.

question: Tribal leader Birsa was associated with which tribe?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Munda.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Birsa Munda (1875–1900) was a tribal freedom fighter and religious leader belonging to the Munda tribe of the Chhotanagpur plateau (present-day Jharkhand). (बिरसा मुंडा — मुंडा जनजाति)

• He led the Ulgulan ("The Great Tumult") movement, 1899–1900, against British land policies, forced labour (begari) and the exploitation of tribals by dikus (outsiders) and moneylenders.

• His followers revered him as "Dharti Aaba" (Father of the Earth) and as Bhagwan Birsa.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Birsa Munda died in Ranchi jail on 9 June 1900. His struggle contributed to the passing of the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act, 1908, which restricted the transfer of tribal land to non-tribals.

• 15 November, his birth anniversary, is observed as Janjatiya Gaurav Divas (Tribal Pride Day); it is also the foundation day of Jharkhand (created in 2000).

• The Bhils are concentrated in Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat; the Gonds mainly in Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Maharashtra; the Bhutias in Sikkim and northern West Bengal.

NOTE

• Other major tribal uprisings: Santhal Rebellion (1855–56) led by Sidhu and Kanhu; Kol Uprising (1831–32); Rampa Rebellion (1922–24) led by Alluri Sitarama Raju; Tana Bhagat movement (1914) led by Jatra Bhagat.

question: Which among the following novels was written by famous Indian author Mulk Raj Anand?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Untouchable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Untouchable" (1935) is the celebrated first novel of Mulk Raj Anand. It portrays a single day in the life of Bakha, a young sweeper, and exposes the cruelty of untouchability and the caste system. (अछूत — मुल्क राज आनंद)

• The novel carried a preface by the English poet E. M. Forster and made Anand one of the pioneers of Indian writing in English.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "The Room on the Roof" was written by Ruskin Bond; it won the John Llewellyn Rhys Prize in 1957 when Bond was only 21.

• Option 3 "Train to Pakistan" (1956) was written by Khushwant Singh and depicts the horrors of the Partition of 1947 in the fictional village of Mano Majra.

• Option 4 "Godan" (1936) is the masterpiece of Munshi Premchand, written in Hindi, about the peasant Hori and rural indebtedness.

NOTE

• Other works of Mulk Raj Anand: Coolie (1936), Two Leaves and a Bud (1937), The Village, Across the Black Waters, The Sword and the Sickle, The Private Life of an Indian Prince.

• Anand, R. K. Narayan and Raja Rao are together called the "trinity" of early Indian English fiction. Anand received the Padma Bhushan in 1968.

question: Rural Backyard Piggery Scheme was launched by which state government?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Meghalaya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Rural Backyard Piggery Scheme was launched by the Government of Meghalaya to support landless and marginal families by providing them with piglets and inputs for rearing pigs in their backyards. (मेघालय — ग्रामीण बैकयार्ड सूकर पालन योजना)

• The aim is to raise household income, nutrition and self-employment in rural areas, since pork is a staple food and pig rearing is a traditional livelihood in Meghalaya and the North-East.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Meghalaya ("the abode of clouds") was carved out of Assam and became a full state on 21 January 1972. Its capital is Shillong.

• Meghalaya is famous for Cherrapunji (Sohra) and Mawsynram, among the wettest places on Earth, and for its living root bridges.

• The state's main tribes are the Khasi, Jaintia and Garo, all of which follow a matrilineal system of inheritance.

NOTE

• Related national livestock schemes: National Livestock Mission, Rashtriya Gokul Mission (indigenous cattle), Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF) and the National Animal Disease Control Programme.

question: Which sea separates Africa from the Arabian peninsula?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Red Sea.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Red Sea is a narrow inlet of the Indian Ocean lying between north-eastern Africa (Egypt, Sudan, Eritrea, Djibouti) and the Arabian Peninsula (Saudi Arabia, Yemen). (लाल सागर)

• It is connected to the Mediterranean Sea in the north through the Suez Canal and to the Arabian Sea / Gulf of Aden in the south through the strait of Bab-el-Mandeb.

• The Red Sea occupies part of the Great Rift Valley system and is one of the saltiest and warmest seas in the world, because it receives almost no river water and suffers high evaporation.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Black Sea lies between Eastern Europe and Western Asia, connected to the Mediterranean by the Bosphorus Strait, Sea of Marmara and Dardanelles.

• The White Sea is an inlet of the Arctic Ocean on the north-western coast of Russia (port of Arkhangelsk).

• The Caspian Sea, bordered by Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran and Azerbaijan, is the largest inland water body (lake) in the world.

NOTE

• The Suez Canal (opened 1869, in Egypt) links the Red Sea with the Mediterranean and is one of the world's busiest shipping routes.

• The Red Sea gets its name from seasonal blooms of the reddish alga Trichodesmium erythraeum.

question: Which among the following terms means growing of fruits?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pomiculture.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Pomiculture" is the cultivation of fruits — the science and practice of growing fruit crops. (फल उत्पादन)

◦ It comes from the Latin pomum meaning "fruit". It is also called fruit culture and is a branch of horticulture.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Apiculture = the rearing of honey bees for honey and wax. (मधुमक्खी पालन)

• Option 2 Arboriculture = the cultivation and care of trees and shrubs, especially for ornamental purposes. (वृक्ष संवर्धन)

• Option 4 Sericulture = the rearing of silkworms for the production of raw silk. (रेशम कीट पालन)

NOTE

• Other "-culture" terms frequently asked in SSC:

◦ Horticulture — growing of garden crops (fruits, vegetables, flowers)

◦ Floriculture — growing of flowers

◦ Olericulture — growing of vegetables

◦ Viticulture — growing of grapes

◦ Pisciculture — rearing of fish

◦ Aquaculture — farming of aquatic organisms

◦ Vermiculture — rearing of earthworms for compost

question: “Chhath Puja” is celebrated with great grandeur all over the world mainly by which community?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihari community.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Chhath Puja is a four-day festival dedicated to the Sun God (Surya) and his sister Chhathi Maiya (Usha), celebrated chiefly by the Bihari community and by people of eastern Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand and the Nepal Terai. (छठ पूजा — बिहार)

• It is observed on the Shashthi (sixth day) of the Hindu month of Kartika (October–November); a smaller Chaiti Chhath falls in the month of Chaitra.

• The four days are Nahay-Khay, Kharna (Lohanda), Sandhya Arghya (offering to the setting sun) and Usha Arghya (offering to the rising sun) — Chhath is the only festival in which the setting sun is also worshipped.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Devotees observe a rigorous fast, often without even water (nirjala), and stand in rivers or ponds to offer arghya.

• With the migration of Bihari families, Chhath is now celebrated in Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Mauritius, Fiji, Trinidad, Guyana, Suriname and the USA.

NOTE

• Other major regional festivals for SSC: Bihu (Assam), Onam (Kerala), Pongal (Tamil Nadu), Baisakhi (Punjab), Gudi Padwa (Maharashtra), Bihula and Sama-Chakeva (Bihar), Hornbill Festival (Nagaland).

question: Shri Bhagwant Mann became the Chief Minister of which state in March 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Punjab.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bhagwant Mann of the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) was sworn in as the Chief Minister of Punjab on 16 March 2022. (भगवंत मान — पंजाब के मुख्यमंत्री)

• He took the oath at Khatkar Kalan, the ancestral village of Shaheed Bhagat Singh, in Shaheed Bhagat Singh Nagar district.

• In the 2022 Punjab Assembly elections, AAP won 92 of the 117 seats, a landslide that ended the Congress government led by Charanjit Singh Channi. Mann himself won from the Dhuri constituency.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Before entering politics as a leader, Bhagwant Mann was a well-known comedian; he had earlier been a Member of Parliament from Sangrur (2014 and 2019).

• Punjab: capital Chandigarh (shared with Haryana), 117 Assembly seats, 13 Lok Sabha seats, 7 Rajya Sabha seats.

• Governor of Punjab at the time of the swearing-in: Banwarilal Purohit.

NOTE

• Other results of the 2022 Assembly elections: Yogi Adityanath returned as CM of Uttar Pradesh, Pushkar Singh Dhami in Uttarakhand, Pramod Sawant in Goa and N. Biren Singh in Manipur.

question: England lift the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2022 trophy after beating ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pakistan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• England won the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2022 by defeating Pakistan by 5 wickets in the final played at the Melbourne Cricket Ground (MCG), Australia, on 13 November 2022. (इंग्लैंड ने पाकिस्तान को हराया)

• Pakistan scored 137/8; England chased it down in 19 overs. Ben Stokes made an unbeaten 52 and Sam Curran took 3/12, winning both the Player of the Match and Player of the Tournament awards.

• England were captained by Jos Buttler; Pakistan by Babar Azam.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• With this win, England became the first team to hold the ODI World Cup (2019) and the T20 World Cup (2022) at the same time. It was England's second T20 World Cup title (the first was in 2010).

• India lost to England by 10 wickets in the semi-final; New Zealand lost to Pakistan in the other semi-final.

• The 2021 T20 World Cup was won by Australia (beating New Zealand); the 2024 edition was won by India (beating South Africa).

NOTE

• T20 World Cup winners: 2007 India, 2009 Pakistan, 2010 England, 2012 West Indies, 2014 Sri Lanka, 2016 West Indies, 2021 Australia, 2022 England, 2024 India.

question: Which two head rivers merge to form the river Ganga?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alaknanda and Bhagirathi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Ganga is formed by the confluence of the Bhagirathi and the Alaknanda at Devprayag in Uttarakhand; downstream of Devprayag the river is called the Ganga. (देवप्रयाग — भागीरथी + अलकनंदा = गंगा)

• The Bhagirathi rises from the Gaumukh snout of the Gangotri glacier; the Alaknanda rises near the Satopanth and Bhagirath Kharak glaciers above Badrinath.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Panch Prayag (five confluences) of the Alaknanda in Uttarakhand:

◦ Vishnuprayag — Alaknanda + Dhauliganga

◦ Nandprayag — Alaknanda + Nandakini

◦ Karnaprayag — Alaknanda + Pindar

◦ Rudraprayag — Alaknanda + Mandakini

◦ Devprayag — Alaknanda + Bhagirathi (the Ganga is born here)

• The Ganga is about 2,525 km long; it enters the plains at Haridwar and forms, with the Brahmaputra and Meghna, the world's largest delta, the Sundarbans.

NOTE

• Major left-bank tributaries of the Ganga: Ramganga, Gomti, Ghaghara, Gandak, Kosi, Mahananda. Major right-bank tributaries: Yamuna, Son, Punpun.

• The Ganga was declared India's National River in 2008; the Namami Gange programme was launched in 2014.

question: Which among the following acids is found in Mustard oil?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Erucic Acid.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Erucic acid is a long-chain monounsaturated omega-9 fatty acid that occurs naturally in mustard oil and rapeseed oil, where it may form 40–50 per cent of the total fatty acids. (सरसों के तेल में इरूसिक अम्ल)

• In large amounts erucic acid is considered harmful to the heart, which is why low-erucic-acid rapeseed (canola) varieties were developed.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 Malic acid is found in apples and other fruits (Latin malum = apple).

• Option 2 Tartaric acid is found in tamarind and grapes; it is a component of baking powder.

• Option 3 Lauric acid is found chiefly in coconut oil and palm kernel oil.

NOTE

• Common natural acids asked in SSC:

◦ Citric acid — lemon, orange

◦ Acetic acid — vinegar

◦ Lactic acid — curd/milk, and in muscles during fatigue

◦ Oxalic acid — tomato, spinach

◦ Formic acid — ant sting and nettle

◦ Butyric acid — rancid butter

◦ Uric acid — urine (excess causes gout)

question: What is the atomic number of Nitrogen in the science periodic table?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 7.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Nitrogen (N) has the atomic number 7, meaning each nitrogen atom contains 7 protons in its nucleus. Its atomic mass is about 14 u, so it also has 7 neutrons in its commonest isotope. (नाइट्रोजन — परमाणु क्रमांक 7)

• Electronic configuration: 2, 5 — it therefore lies in Group 15 (VA) and Period 2 of the modern periodic table.

• Nitrogen makes up about 78 per cent of the Earth's atmosphere by volume and exists as the very stable diatomic molecule N₂ with a triple bond.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 21 is the atomic number of Scandium (Sc).

• Option 3 18 is the atomic number of Argon (Ar), a noble gas.

• Option 4 11 is the atomic number of Sodium (Na).

NOTE

• Atomic numbers worth memorising: H = 1, He = 2, C = 6, N = 7, O = 8, F = 9, Ne = 10, Na = 11, Mg = 12, Al = 13, Si = 14, P = 15, S = 16, Cl = 17, Ar = 18, K = 19, Ca = 20.

• Nitrogen was discovered by Daniel Rutherford (1772). Liquid nitrogen (boiling point −196 °C) is used as a cryogenic coolant, and nitrogen is essential for making ammonia (Haber process) and fertilisers such as urea.

question: Kuchipudi dance is accompanied by which type of music?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Carnatic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Kuchipudi, the classical dance of Andhra Pradesh, is performed to Carnatic music, the classical music tradition of South India. (कुचिपुड़ी — कर्नाटक संगीत)

• The accompanying instruments typically include the mridangam, violin, veena, flute and cymbals (talam), with a vocalist singing in Telugu or Sanskrit.

• Kuchipudi takes its name from the village of Kuchelapuram in Krishna district; it was systematised in the 17th century by Siddhendra Yogi, whose famous dance-drama is Bhama Kalapam.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• A signature item of Kuchipudi is the Tarangam, in which the dancer performs while balancing a pot of water on the head and dancing on the rim of a brass plate.

• Famous exponents: Vempati Chinna Satyam, Raja and Radha Reddy, Yamini Krishnamurthy, Shobha Naidu, Swapnasundari.

NOTE

• Classical dances and their music:

◦ Carnatic music — Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kathakali (Kerala)

◦ Hindustani music — Kathak (North India), Odissi is accompanied by Odissi music, Manipuri by Manipuri traditions, and Sattriya by Assamese Borgeet.

question: In which country was the first Olympic Games held in the year 1896?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Greece.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece, from 6 to 15 April 1896. (यूनान — प्रथम आधुनिक ओलंपिक)

• They were organised at the initiative of the French educationist Baron Pierre de Coubertin, who founded the International Olympic Committee (IOC) in 1894 at the Sorbonne, Paris.

• About 241 athletes from 14 nations took part in 43 events across 9 sports. The main venue was the restored Panathenaic Stadium.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The ancient Olympic Games began in 776 BCE at Olympia in Greece in honour of Zeus and were abolished in 393 CE by Emperor Theodosius I.

• The first Olympic champion of the modern era was James Connolly (USA, triple jump). Greece's Spyridon Louis won the first marathon.

• The Olympic motto is "Citius, Altius, Fortius — Communiter" (Faster, Higher, Stronger — Together); the five interlocking rings represent the five inhabited continents.

NOTE

• The IOC headquarters is at Lausanne, Switzerland. Recent Summer Olympics: 2016 Rio de Janeiro, 2020 Tokyo (held in 2021), 2024 Paris; the 2028 Games go to Los Angeles.

question: Who is the playback singer and composer of the famous song “Qismat Ki Hawa” which featured in the movie Ludo in 2020?
solution_text:
The correct answer is C. Ramchandra.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The song "Qismat Ki Hawa Kabhi Naram Kabhi Garam" was composed and sung by C. Ramchandra for the film Albela (1951), and it was reused in Anurag Basu's 2020 film Ludo. (सी. रामचंद्र)

• C. Ramchandra (Ramchandra Narhar Chitalkar, 1918–1982) was a leading music director of the 1940s–50s who also sang under the name Chitalkar.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• His most famous composition is the patriotic song "Aye Mere Watan Ke Logon" (lyrics by Kavi Pradeep), sung by Lata Mangeshkar before Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru in 1963.

• Other well-known songs from Albela (1951): "Bholi Surat Dil Ke Khote", "Sham Dhale Khidki Tale", "Dheere Se Aaja Ri Akhiyan Mein".

• Ludo (2020) was directed by Anurag Basu and starred Abhishek Bachchan, Rajkummar Rao, Pankaj Tripathi, Aditya Roy Kapur and Fatima Sana Shaikh; it was released on Netflix.

NOTE

• Distractors: Arijit Singh is a contemporary playback singer ("Tum Hi Ho"); A. R. Rahman is an Oscar-winning composer ("Jai Ho"); R. D. Burman (Pancham) was the celebrated composer of the 1970s–80s ("Dum Maro Dum", "Piya Tu Ab To Aaja").

question: Guru Vempati Chinna Satyam is associated with which of the following dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kuchipudi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Vempati Chinna Satyam (1929–2012) was the most celebrated guru of Kuchipudi, the classical dance of Andhra Pradesh. (वेम्पति चिन्ना सत्यम — कुचिपुड़ी)

• He founded the Kuchipudi Art Academy in Chennai (1963) and took Kuchipudi from village dance-drama to the international solo concert stage, choreographing more than 180 solo items and 15 dance-dramas.

• He was honoured with the Padma Bhushan (1998) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1967).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Famous exponents of other forms:

◦ Kathak — Birju Maharaj, Sitara Devi, Shambhu Maharaj, Lachhu Maharaj

◦ Bharatanatyam — Rukmini Devi Arundale, Balasaraswati, Yamini Krishnamurthy, Padma Subrahmanyam

◦ Manipuri — Guru Bipin Singh, Nirmala Mehta, Jhaveri Sisters

• Kuchipudi originated in the village of Kuchelapuram (Krishna district, Andhra Pradesh) and was revived by Siddhendra Yogi.

NOTE

• The eight classical dances recognised by the Sangeet Natak Akademi: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (Uttar Pradesh), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question: Rural Employment Generation Programme (REGP) was launched in ________ .
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1995.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Rural Employment Generation Programme (REGP) was launched in 1995 and was implemented by the Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC). (ग्रामीण रोजगार सृजन कार्यक्रम — 1995)

• Its objective was to create self-employment opportunities in rural areas and small towns by helping entrepreneurs set up village industries, with margin-money subsidy and bank credit.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• In 2008, REGP was merged with the Prime Minister's Rozgar Yojana (PMRY) to form the Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP), a credit-linked subsidy scheme administered by the Ministry of MSME through KVIC as the nodal agency.

• KVIC was established in 1956 under the Khadi and Village Industries Commission Act, with headquarters in Mumbai.

NOTE

• Other landmark employment/rural schemes and their years: IRDP (1978–79), JRY (1989), EAS (1993), SGSY (1999), SGRY (2001), NREGA/MGNREGA (2005, renamed 2009), NRLM–Aajeevika (2011), DDU-GKY (2014), PMEGP (2008).

question: Jyotiba Phule founded which of the following organizations?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Satyashodhak Samaj.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Jyotirao (Jyotiba) Govindrao Phule (1827–1890) founded the Satyashodhak Samaj ("Society of Truth Seekers") at Pune on 24 September 1873. (सत्यशोधक समाज — ज्योतिबा फुले)

• Its aims were to liberate the Shudras and Ati-Shudras from caste oppression and Brahminical domination, to promote education among the lower castes and women, and to make rituals simple and priest-free.

• Along with his wife Savitribai Phule — regarded as India's first woman teacher — he opened the first school for girls in Pune in 1848 and a home for widows and their children.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Phule's famous works: Gulamgiri (1873), Shetkaryacha Asud (Cultivator's Whipcord), Tritiya Ratna and Sarvajanik Satyadharma Pustak. He was given the title "Mahatma" in 1888 by Vithalrao Krishnaji Vandekar.

• Arya Samaj was founded by Swami Dayanand Saraswati in 1875 at Bombay, with the slogan "Back to the Vedas".

• Brahmo Samaj was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828 at Calcutta.

• The Satnami movement was led by Ghasidas in Chhattisgarh (an earlier Satnami sect was founded by Birbhan in the 17th century).

NOTE

• Other social-reform bodies for SSC: Prarthana Samaj (Atmaram Pandurang, 1867), Ramakrishna Mission (Swami Vivekananda, 1897), Servants of India Society (Gopal Krishna Gokhale, 1905), Self-Respect Movement (E. V. Ramasamy 'Periyar', 1925).

question: Jeev Milkha Singh is associated with which sport?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Golf.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Jeev Milkha Singh (born 15 December 1971) is a leading Indian professional golfer. (जीव मिल्खा सिंह — गोल्फ)

• He was the first Indian golfer to join the European Tour and the first Indian to play in all four major championships. He has won four European Tour titles and topped the Asian Tour Order of Merit in 2006 and 2008.

• He received the Arjuna Award (1999) and the Padma Shri (2007).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• He is the son of the legendary sprinter Milkha Singh, the "Flying Sikh", who won gold at the 1958 Commonwealth Games and 1958 & 1962 Asian Games and finished fourth in the 400 m at the 1960 Rome Olympics.

• Other well-known Indian golfers: Anirban Lahiri, Shubhankar Sharma, Gaganjeet Bhullar, Arjun Atwal, Aditi Ashok (who finished fourth at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics).

NOTE

• Golf terms often asked: birdie (one under par), eagle (two under par), albatross (three under par), bogey (one over par), par, caddie, tee, putt, fairway, green.

• The four golf majors: The Masters, PGA Championship, U.S. Open and The Open Championship (British Open).

question: Cotton was probably grown at Mehrgarh from about ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 7000 years ago.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mehrgarh, a Neolithic site on the Kacchi plain of Balochistan (present-day Pakistan), near the Bolan Pass, is the place where cotton was probably grown about 7,000 years ago. (मेहरगढ़ — लगभग 7000 वर्ष पूर्व कपास)

• NCERT history textbooks describe Mehrgarh as one of the earliest villages in the subcontinent, where people first began to grow wheat and barley and to rear sheep, goats and cattle.

• Mehrgarh was excavated by the French archaeologist Jean-François Jarrige from 1974 onwards.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Burials at Mehrgarh show the dead placed with goats and beads, indicating belief in an afterlife; the site also yielded evidence of the world's earliest known dentistry (drilled teeth).

• Cotton later became a hallmark of the Harappan civilisation; actual cotton cloth fragments have been found at Mohenjo-daro, and cotton seeds at Mehrgarh. The Greeks called Indian cotton "sindon".

NOTE

• Key Harappan sites: Harappa (Ravi, Pakistan), Mohenjo-daro (Indus, Pakistan), Lothal (Gujarat — dockyard), Dholavira (Gujarat — water management, UNESCO site), Kalibangan (Rajasthan — ploughed field), Rakhigarhi (Haryana — largest Indian site), Banawali and Surkotada (horse bones).

question: Which among the following are called the amphibians of the plant kingdom?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bryophyte.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bryophytes — the mosses, liverworts and hornworts — are called the "amphibians of the plant kingdom" because although they live on land, they require water for sexual reproduction, since their motile male gametes (antherozoids) must swim to the egg. (ब्रायोफाइटा — पादप जगत के उभयचर)

• They lack true roots, stems and leaves and have no vascular tissue (no xylem or phloem); they are anchored by rhizoids.

• Examples: Funaria (moss), Marchantia and Riccia (liverworts), Sphagnum (bog moss, used as packing material and a source of peat).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Thallophyta (Option 3) are the simplest plants — algae and, in older classifications, fungi — with an undifferentiated thallus body.

• Gymnosperms (Option 1) are naked-seeded vascular plants such as Pinus, Cycas and Cedrus.

• Angiosperms (Option 4) are flowering plants whose seeds are enclosed in fruits; they are divided into monocots and dicots.

NOTE

• Whittaker's classification of the plant kingdom: Thallophyta → Bryophyta → Pteridophyta → Gymnosperms → Angiosperms.

• Pteridophytes (ferns) are called the "first true land plants" because they are the first group to possess vascular tissue.

question: The term “Vetti” in Chola empire is related to ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is forced labour.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under the Cholas, "Vetti" was a tax collected not in cash but in the form of forced/unpaid labour demanded from the villagers. (वेट्टि — बेगार / अवैतनिक श्रम)

• Another important Chola levy was "Kadamai", the land revenue paid by cultivators.

• These terms come from Chola inscriptions, especially those of Rajaraja I and Rajendra I, and are part of the NCERT chapter on new kings and kingdoms.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Cholas ruled from Thanjavur (Tanjore) in the Kaveri delta; the dynasty was founded in the 9th century by Vijayalaya Chola (c. 850 CE).

• Rajaraja I (985–1014 CE) built the Brihadeeswarar (Rajarajeshwara) temple at Thanjavur, a UNESCO World Heritage Site among the "Great Living Chola Temples".

• Rajendra I conquered up to the Ganga, took the title Gangaikonda Chola and built the new capital Gangaikonda Cholapuram; he also sent naval expeditions to Srivijaya (South-East Asia).

NOTE

• Chola local self-government was famous: the Ur (assembly of ordinary villagers), the Sabha (assembly of Brahmin villages, brahmadeya) and the Nagaram (assembly of merchants). The Uttaramerur inscriptions describe the elaborate election procedure (kudavolai system) of the Sabha's committees.

question: Who chairs the Monetary Policy Committee in India?
option_2: Deputy Governor, Reserve Bank of India
option_3: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
solution_text:
The correct answer is Governor, Reserve Bank of India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of India is chaired by the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India. (भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक के गवर्नर)

• The MPC was constituted in 2016 under the RBI Act, 1934 (as amended by the Finance Act, 2016) and is responsible for fixing the policy repo rate to achieve the inflation target.

• It has six members: three from the RBI — the Governor (Chairperson), the Deputy Governor in charge of monetary policy, and an officer nominated by the Central Board — and three external members appointed by the Central Government for four years.

• Decisions are by majority vote; in case of a tie the Governor has a casting vote. The MPC must meet at least four times a year.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• India's inflation target is 4 per cent CPI inflation with a tolerance band of ±2 per cent (i.e. 2–6 per cent), notified by the Central Government in consultation with the RBI every five years.

• The RBI was established on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934, and was nationalised on 1 January 1949. Its first Governor was Sir Osborne Smith and the first Indian Governor was C. D. Deshmukh.

NOTE

• Key monetary policy tools: Repo rate, Reverse repo rate, Marginal Standing Facility (MSF), Bank rate, Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR), Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) and Open Market Operations (OMO).

question: The Lok Sabha (House of the People) was duly constituted for the first time on ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 17 April 1952.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first Lok Sabha was duly constituted on 17 April 1952, after the country's first general elections, which were held from October 1951 to February 1952. (प्रथम लोकसभा — 17 अप्रैल 1952)

• The first sitting of the House was held on 13 May 1952. Its first Speaker was G. V. Mavalankar, and the first Prime Minister of the elected House was Jawaharlal Nehru.

• The first Lok Sabha had 489 seats, of which the Indian National Congress won 364. India's first Chief Election Commissioner was Sukumar Sen.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Before 1952, the Constituent Assembly (which had adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949) served as the provisional Parliament of India.

• The Lok Sabha's maximum strength as per the Constitution is 552 (530 from States + 20 from Union Territories + 2 Anglo-Indians, the last category discontinued by the 104th Amendment, 2019). Present strength: 543.

• The normal term of the Lok Sabha is five years, extendable by one year at a time during a National Emergency.

NOTE

• Related dates: the Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 (Constitution Day) and came into force on 26 January 1950 (Republic Day). The Rajya Sabha was first constituted on 3 April 1952.
